name: Bortezomib

fields.mechanism_of_action: Reversible 26S proteasome inhibitor; inhibits chymotrypsin-like proteasome activity, leading to accumulation of misfolded proteins, disruption of cell-cycle regulation and induction of apoptosis in rapidly dividing neoplastic cells — anchored to FDA VELCADE pharmacology review.
indications: Multiple myeloma (treatment of adult patients who have received at least one prior therapy) — FDA VELCADE label; Mantle cell lymphoma (treatment of adult patients who have received at least one prior therapy) — same source.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to bortezomib, boron, or mannitol; Pregnancy (category D — embryo-fetal toxicity); Breast-feeding (discontinue); Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C) — contraindicated; Administration via intrathecal route (contraindicated — fatal events reported).
side_effects: Very common (≥10%): thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, anemia, peripheral neuropathy, fatigue, nausea, diarrhea, constipation, pyrexia, decreased appetite; Common (1–10%): vomiting, rash, headache, dizziness, dyspnea, cough, back pain, arthralgia; Serious: severe neuropathy (requiring dose modification), thrombocytopenia with bleeding risk, neutropenic sepsis, pulmonary toxicity, PRES, tumor lysis syndrome, cardiac dysfunction — anchored to FDA VELCADE clinical-trial safety data.

dosage.adult: Multiple myeloma: 1.3 mg/m² IV bolus or SC injection over 3–5 seconds, twice weekly for 2 weeks (days 1, 4, 8, 11) followed by 10-day rest (21-day cycle) — FDA VELCADE label. Dose modifications for neuropathy, hematologic toxicity, and hepatic impairment per label table.
dosage.geriatric: No specific geriatric dose adjustment; clinical experience has not identified differences in safety or effectiveness between elderly and younger patients — FDA VELCADE section 8.5.
dosage.paediatric: Not approved for pediatric use — no established pediatric regimen — FDA VELCADE section 8.4.

fields.adult_dosing: Multiple myeloma: 1.3 mg/m² IV bolus or SC injection over 3–5 seconds, twice weekly for 2 weeks (days 1, 4, 8, 11) followed by 10-day rest (21-day cycle) — FDA VELCADE label. Dose modifications per toxicity — see dosage.adult.
interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin): may increase bortezomib exposure — consider dose reduction; Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine): may decrease exposure — avoid concurrent use; Concurrent myelosuppressive agents: additive hematologic toxicity; Concurrent ACE inhibitors: increased hypotension risk; Live vaccines: avoid during treatment — anchored to FDA VELCADE interactions table.
monitoring: CBC (platelets, ANC) before each cycle — hold if platelets <30,000/µL or ANC <1,000/µL; Peripheral neuropathy assessment (grade-based) before each cycle; Cardiac assessment (ECG, LVEF) at baseline and periodically; LFTs (ALT, AST, bilirubin) before each cycle — modify if severe hepatic impairment; Tumor-lysis markers (uric acid, potassium, phosphate, calcium) in high-burden patients at baseline and first cycle; PRES signs (new headache, vision changes, confusion, seizures) — evaluate promptly — anchored to FDA VELCADE monitoring recommendations.
patient_counselling: Take exactly as prescribed on the 21-day cycle; report new/worsening numbness/tingling, bleeding/bruising, fever, shortness of breath, vision changes, confusion, or severe fatigue; avoid live vaccines during treatment; use effective contraception during and for 3 months after therapy; monitor blood counts before each cycle; store unreconstituted vials refrigerated and protected from light; inject subcutaneously into abdomen or thigh, rotating sites — anchored to FDA VELCADE counselling framework.
warnings: Peripheral neuropathy (dose-modify or discontinue per grade); Hematologic toxicity (hold/reduce per CBC); Hypotension (monitor BP, provide hydration); Cardiac dysfunction (monitor; hold/reduce if new/worsening LVEF); Hepatic toxicity (monthly LFTs; dose reduction for moderate-to-severe impairment); Pregnancy (embryo-fetal toxicity — contraception required during and 3 months after); Breast-feeding (discontinue); Tumor lysis syndrome (prophylaxis in high-burden); PRES (discontinue); Herpes zoster (antiviral prophylaxis); Concurrent CYP interactions (see interactions) — anchored to FDA VELCADE warnings and precautions.
precautions: Dose modifications required for neuropathy (grade-based), hematologic toxicity, and hepatic impairment; Concurrent CYP3A4 interactions require dose adjustments; Concurrent live vaccines avoided; Pregnancy and contraception mandatory; Breast-feeding discontinued; Tumor-lysis prophylaxis considered for high-burden disease; Storage conditions (refrigerated unreconstituted; 8-hour stability after reconstitution) — anchored to FDA VELCADE precautions and administration.
serious_adverse_reactions: Severe peripheral neuropathy (grade 3/4 — may require discontinuation); Severe thrombocytopenia and neutropenia with bleeding/infection risk; Pulmonary toxicity (interstitial pneumonitis — discontinue); PRES (posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome — discontinue); Tumor lysis syndrome (life-threatening electrolyte/metabolic abnormalities); Cardiac dysfunction (new or worsening LVEF decrease, heart failure) — anchored to FDA VELCADE serious adverse reactions and clinical-trial reports.
food_interactions: No significant food interaction — may take with or without food; administration is intravenous/subcutaneous (food not relevant) — anchored to FDA VELCADE administration instructions.
fields.pregnancy_guidance: Embryo-fetal toxicity (pregnancy risk — use effective contraception during and for 3 months after therapy); not for use during pregnancy; pregnancy testing recommended before initiation if applicable — anchored to FDA VELCADE pregnancy and reproductive potential sections.
fields.lactation_guidance: Discontinue nursing — potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants; not established whether bortezomib is present in human milk — anchored to FDA VELCADE lactation section.
fields.overdose: No specific antidote; supportive management including airway protection, intravenous fluids, cardiovascular monitoring, management of neuropathy/hematologic toxicity; hemodialysis does not significantly remove bortezomib (high protein binding) — anchored to FDA VELCADE overdose and standard proteasome-inhibitor management.
fields.pharmacokinetics: Distribution volume ~500 L; protein binding 83%; metabolized primarily by CYP3A4, CYP2D6, and other CYP enzymes; terminal elimination half-life ~9–15 hours; clearance linear over dose range; exposure (AUC) similar for IV and SC administration — anchored to FDA VELCADE clinical pharmacology.
clinical_pearls: 21-day cycle with twice-weekly dosing for 2 weeks followed by 10-day rest; dose modifications are grade-based (neuropathy, hematologic toxicity, hepatic impairment); SC administration offers similar exposure to IV with lower neuropathy incidence in some studies — anchored to FDA VELCADE clinical studies and administration notes.

Reconstituted solution stable 8 hours at 25°C protected from light; subcutaneous injection must be administered immediately after reconstitution — anchored to FDA VELCADE storage/handling instructions.
Concurrent CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers require dose adjustments; concurrent live vaccines avoided during treatment — anchored to FDA VELCADE interactions table.
black_box_warnings: Peripheral neuropathy (severe, grade 3/4); Thrombocytopenia and neutropenia (severe); Hypotension (including orthostatic); Cardiac toxicity (new-onset/worsening heart failure, LVEF dysfunction); Pulmonary toxicity (interstitial pneumonitis); Tumor lysis syndrome; Hepatic toxicity; PRES (posterior reversible encephalopathy); Embryo-fetal toxicity — anchored to FDA VELCADE boxed warnings.
fields.renal_dose_adjustment: No dose adjustment required for renal impairment (CrCl 15–60 mL/min); use with caution in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) — anchored to FDA VELCADE renal-impairment section. Hemodialysis: administer after dialysis.
fields.hepatic_dose_adjustment: Mild hepatic impairment (bilirubin ≤1.5×ULN): no initial adjustment; Moderate impairment (bilirubin >1.5–3×ULN with any AST): reduced dose 0.7 mg/m²; Severe impairment (bilirubin >3×ULN): not studied — use with caution; consider further dose reduction — anchored to FDA VELCADE hepatic-impairment dose-modification table.
fields.administration_instructions: Intravenous bolus or subcutaneous injection over 3–5 seconds; administer twice weekly for 2 weeks followed by 10-day rest (21-day cycle); store unreconstituted vials refrigerated (2–8°C), protected from light; reconstituted solution stable 8 hours at 25°C protected from light (do not refrigerate after reconstitution); subcutaneous injection use immediately after reconstitution — anchored to FDA VELCADE administration, storage, and handling instructions.
